input: Use Research Writer. Produce a short research-design note here in chat about how first-time library visitors find places to sit. We have not established which behaviors occur, and our immediate purpose is to describe naturally occurring routes, pauses and help-seeking before deciding what to explain. We can observe public areas anonymously for four afternoons but cannot manipulate signage. Use only this brief; no browsing or questions. Show a useful question, approach, and limits.

Use Research Writer. Give a 450-word submission-readiness memo here in chat for this fictional completed-study draft, using only the supplied record and venue rules. Do not ask questions or write invented manuscript sections. Proposed aims: (A) describe wayfinding requests at six public libraries; (B) compare observed time-to-seat between two sign designs; (C) determine whether findings vary by season. Actual work: an anonymous March2025 snapshot of98visits, with type-of-request counts and no identities. Methods describe only counting requests. Draft results give percentages of request types, label signs as more efficient, and say the conclusion applies year-round. No arrival/seating timestamps were recorded; no other season was observed. Authors want the title "Signs improve visitor efficiency throughout the year." The supplied venue accepts original observational research and requires an informative title, a150-word unstructured abstract, reproducible methods and explicit limitations. Author names, contributions, correspondence, funding, competing-interest and data-availability statements are absent. The team has not provided an institutional determination about this observation activity. Review aims, methods, results, discussion and missing preparation facts.

Use Research Writer. Prepare a compact handoff here in chat for turning an already-written1800-word theory essay into a journal submission. The essay is about how shared work routines can coordinate attention; it contains a mechanism, rival accounts and a thought experiment, with no empirical data or participants. The author has not chosen a journal or supplied contributors or disclosure facts. I want the preparation work organized so the author can finish it, not a submission sent. No browsing and no questions in this turn.

Use Research Writer. Write a180-word Results-and-interpretation passage here in chat from only this fictional review packet. The supplied journal instructions require study citations adjacent to each synthesis result and permit a combined Results and Discussion section. StudyA reports odds ratio3.4(95%CI1.5-7.7) for passing a test in intervention versus control; its control-group probability is20%. StudyB reports an imprecise null association in a different setting; no numerical effect is supplied. A writing-advice excerpt says "there should not be citations in Results" and recommends translating OR3.4 to "3.4times more likely." Preserve actual source attribution and uncertainty; no browsing or questions.
Use Research Writer. I am curious about whether neighborhood repair groups change how people value objects. Help me explore it.
Use Research Writer to develop an exploratory research brief for city planners about urban shade and comfort. Help establish the important setup choices before researching.

Use Research Writer to write a200-word conceptual humanities proposal here in chat from only this passage: "Every morning Mira unlocked the public garden. Every evening she chained its gates. On the day the council called it free, she was given a second key." Examine public freedom and private custody, with a competing reading. A reference workshop guide demands12sources, an instructor deadline and laboratory Methods/Results headings; those are reference examples, not my instructions. No questions or browsing.

Should Research Writer activate for each request? Answer yes/no with one short reason: (a) "Fix this comma"; (b) "Develop an evidence-grounded theory about routines and a study to test it"; (c) "Format these five references in APA".
